title.value: Challenging Common Assumptions about Catastrophic Forgetting
title.justification: The title was identified from the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: C HALLENGING C OMMON A SSUMPTIONS ABOUT C ATASTROPHIC F ORGETTING

extractions.description: The paper investigates the phenomenon of catastrophic forgetting in deep neural networks (DNNs) and proposes a new framework, SCoLe, to study knowledge accumulation (KA) in continual learning scenarios. It challenges the prevailing belief that catastrophic forgetting prevents knowledge accumulation, showing that DNNs can retain and accumulate knowledge over long sequences of tasks when data re-occurrence is present. The study explores strategies to improve knowledge accumulation, such as gradient masking and replay mechanisms.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving the performance of neural networks in continual learning scenarios by studying knowledge accumulation and catastrophic forgetting. It does not directly address climate or ecological sustainability issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our contributions are as follows: We first show that forgetting does not prevent the transfer to downstream tasks, even several tasks later. We call this effect “knowledge retention”, and we show it leads to knowledge accumulation when tasks are reoccurring.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on any specific Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category. It centers on the mechanics of deep learning algorithms, specifically addressing catastrophic forgetting and knowledge accumulation.
primary_category.quote: SCoLe scenarios are in between IID scenarios and usual CL scenarios, as the data may reoccur, but the distribution changes through time.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not cover secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes. It is focused exclusively on machine learning issues related to continual learning.
secondary_categories.quote: Continual learning (CL) aims to design algorithms that learn from non-stationary sequences of tasks and accumulate knowledge.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development is relevant to the technological focus of this paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose SCoLe (Scaling Continual Learning), a framework that allows the generation of long sequences of potentially overlapping tasks (Figure 4).

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not include secondary sub-categories relevant to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We investigate different strategies to improve knowledge accumulation effects, such as gradient masking, frequency replay, optimizing the learning-forgetting trade-off or making models wider.

applications.justification: The paper does not explicitly address applications related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
applications.quote: We challenge this idea and step back from classical CL and CF literature to investigate to which extent fine-tuning with SGD under sequential distribution shifts prevents the model from accumulating knowledge.

new_primary_category.justification: A new Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category is not necessary as the paper does not relate to this field.
new_primary_category.quote: The findings of this paper that DNNs consistently retain and accumulate knowledge could provide an explanation for the observation that self-supervised models are continual learners.

new_primary_sub_category.quote: This paper investigates knowledge retention (KR) and accumulation (KA) in deep neural networks.
